The Alaskan husky is not an officially recognized breed by any [kennel club](/wiki/Kennel_club "Kennel club"), nor does it have a formal breed standard.[[6]](#cite_note-6) Unlike breeds developed for the show ring, the Alaskan husky is instead a product of careful selection for desirable sled dog traits from various other breeds, such as aptitude for pulling, endurance, speed, intelligence, appetite, and tolerance of extreme weather.[[7]](#cite_note-:5-7)[[8]](#cite_note-:6-8) As a result of this specific and mindful performance-only based breeding, DNA studies show that Alaskan Huskies share a genetic signature and indeed can be identified accurately on DNA breed tests.[[9]](#cite_note-:1-9)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Lava_the_sled_dog.jpg/250px-Lava_the_sled_dog.jpg)](/wiki/File:Lava_the_sled_dog.jpg)

Blue-eyed Alaskan husky, a common feature in the Siberian Husky contributor to the breed

The Alaskan husky is a highly athletic dog variety, and as it is a crossbreed, its appearance can vary markedly, although various lines have been bred for multiple generations and still breed very true to their lines' types.[[10]](#cite_note-Morris-10) Some Alaskan husky lines have characteristic [spitz](/wiki/Spitz "Spitz")-like features, such as pointed ears and curled tails, while other lines more closely resemble their [hound](/wiki/Hound "Hound") or [gundog](/wiki/Gundog "Gundog") heritage with tipped or floppy ears, straight tails and tucked up [sighthound](/wiki/Sighthound "Sighthound")-like loins.[[11]](#cite_note-Bonham-11)[[12]](#cite_note-Coppinger-12) As they are not bred with conformation in mind, cosmetic features are not a consideration for breeding, and these features instead tend to follow the purpose of the dog's intended style of sled work.

The red border symbolizes both the Native Americans, who "knew and loved our country long before any of us were here," and the blood of pioneers who gave their lives reclaiming the land. White signifies purity and uprightness, while blue, reminiscent of Wyoming's skies and distant mountains, represents fidelity, justice, and virility. Finally, the pamphlet notes that the red, white, and blue of Wyoming's flag correspond to the colors of the Stars and Stripes of the United States, the "greatest flag in all the world."[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Methionine :: A proteinogenic amino acid :: Encoding :: chunk_0003
Methionine is one of only two amino acids encoded by a single [codon](/wiki/Codon "Codon") (AUG) in the standard [genetic code](/wiki/Genetic_code "Genetic code") ([tryptophan](/wiki/Tryptophan "Tryptophan"), encoded by UGG, is the other). In reflection to the evolutionary origin of its codon, the other AUN codons encode [isoleucine](/wiki/Isoleucine "Isoleucine"), which is also a hydrophobic amino acid. In the mitochondrial genome of several organisms, including [metazoa](/wiki/Vertebrate_mitochondrial_code "Vertebrate mitochondrial code") and [yeast](/wiki/The_yeast_mitochondrial_code "The yeast mitochondrial code"), the codon AUA also encodes for methionine. In the standard genetic code AUA codes for isoleucine and the respective tRNA (*ileX* in *Escherichia coli*) uses the unusual base [lysidine](/wiki/Lysidine_(nucleoside) "Lysidine (nucleoside)") (bacteria) or [agmatidine](/wiki/Agmatidine "Agmatidine") (archaea) to discriminate against AUG.[[13]](#cite_note-13)[[14]](#cite_note-14)

The methionine codon AUG is also the most common start codon. A "Start" codon is message for a [ribosome](/wiki/Ribosome "Ribosome") that signals the initiation of protein [translation](/wiki/Translation_(biology) "Translation (biology)") from mRNA when the AUG codon is in a [Kozak consensus sequence](/wiki/Kozak_consensus_sequence "Kozak consensus sequence"). As a consequence, methionine is often incorporated into the *N*-terminal position of [proteins](/wiki/Protein "Protein") in [eukaryotes](/wiki/Eukaryote "Eukaryote") and [archaea](/wiki/Archaea "Archaea") during translation, although it can be removed by [post-translational modification](/wiki/Post-translational_modification "Post-translational modification"). In [bacteria](/wiki/Bacteria "Bacteria"), the derivative [*N*-formylmethionine](/wiki/N-Formylmethionine "N-Formylmethionine") is used as the initial amino acid.

A mass meeting of the student body was called, and a star player showed up wearing a navy blue and orange scarf he had brought back from a [University of Oxford](/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") summer rowing expedition. The colors were chosen when another student pulled the scarf from the player's neck, waved it to the crowd and yelled: "How will this do?" (Exactly 100 years later in 1988, Oxford named their own American football club the "Cavaliers," and soon after the Virginia team adopted its "curved sabres" logo in 1994, the Oxford team followed suit.)
